clue.text: Funny actor in a common English garment

indicators.note: funny in the sense of peculiar or odd, telling us the letters that follow are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A comic actor turns up in an everyday English item of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' looks like a description of the actor but signals an anagram of ACTOR IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: A mac for wet weather is a staple item of English clothing, worn everywhere.

clue.text: Who, for example, makes a kinsman in favour of a celibate going without love?

parts.note: a relative is a member of the family
pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: going without means one piece wraps round the outside of the other

parts.note: a nun lives under a vow of chastity
O is love, a nil score in tennis

explanation.surface: Asks what makes a family member side with a chaste person lacking romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going without' looks like 'doing without love' but means NUN goes outside O. 'Who' is a grammatical example.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, who, which and that introduce clauses describing a noun, the class of relative pronouns.

clue.text: Not so warm but taking the company to heart

clue.text: Holiday resort-provide a quotation with electricity included

indicators.note: included says the electricity goes inside the word for quoting

parts.note: to cite is to quote a source
amps measure electric current

explanation.surface: Instructions for a holiday site: quote something and supply power.
explanation.definitionFit: A camping ground is a place where holidaymakers stay in tents.

clue.text: Room to be included in that ticket

indicators.note: to be included in tells us the answer lies within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Space in a loft comes with the entry pass.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is a room in the roof space of a house.

clue.text: Well-being is left in an area of open country

indicators.note: the word in says the letter for left goes inside the stretch of open country

parts.note: a heath is uncultivated open land

explanation.surface: A claim that wellness is found out on the open moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: Good health is a state of physical and mental soundness, a synonym of well-being.

clue.text: Cut out tax

definitions.meaning: a duty charged on goods such as alcohol

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to remove by cutting; the other is a duty levied on home-produced goods.

clue.text: Being a rake, the composer gets into a row

indicators.note: gets into puts the composer inside the row

parts.note: a line is a row
Jacques Ibert was a French composer

explanation.surface: A musician starts a quarrel while living dissolutely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel but is LINE; IBERT is the French composer Jacques Ibert.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a dissolute pleasure-seeker, a libertine.

clue.text: The man to pay back goes on the trail for an outlaw

parts.note: he refers to a man
to reward is to repay someone for service
a wake is the trail left behind a moving boat

explanation.surface: A man seeking repayment sets off in pursuit of a bandit.
explanation.walkthrough: Hereward the Wake was an English rebel outlaw who resisted the Norman conquest in the Fens.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereward is the legendary English fugitive who fought William the Conqueror from the Fens, an outlaw hero.

clue.text: The superintendent would be finished if it weren't for the language

indicators.note: if it weren't for says that removing the language from the answer would leave the word for finished, so it sits inside

parts.note: over means finished
Erse is Irish or Scots Gaelic

explanation.surface: A supervisor would be done for, were it not for the tongue he speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: A subtractive description: the 'superintendent' minus the Gaelic tongue would be 'finished', so 'if it weren't for' signals a container read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An overseer is someone who supervises work, a superintendent.

clue.text: Theme which may make the learner move it twice

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate

indicators.note: may make suggests the following words can be reworked into something else, an anagram signal
twice tells us the word it is used two times

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A recurring musical idea that might persuade a pupil to move a piece twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may make' scrambles MOVE plus the doubled IT (ITIT, from 'twice') into EITMOTIV; 'which' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A leitmotif is a recurring musical theme tied to a character or idea, as in Wagner.

clue.text: Large pole caught at mouth of river

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
Aber is a Celtic word for a river mouth, seen in place names such as Aberdeen

explanation.surface: A big pole snagged where a river meets the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: ABER, a Celtic word for a river mouth, is familiar from Welsh and Scottish place names; 'at' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The caber is the long tree trunk tossed at Scottish Highland games, a large wooden pole.

clue.text: School fees?

parts.note: the school year is divided into periods, while conditions of payment or charges are also known by this word

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both divisions of the school year and the agreed charges or conditions of a deal.

clue.text: Sailors from Irish port used to open bottles

parts.note: Cork is a port city in the south of Ireland
sailors from Cork are the port's own crew, so from gives the possessive S
a crew is the body of sailors on a ship

explanation.surface: Seamen from an Irish harbour city were once employed to uncork wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Sailors from Cork are 'Cork's crew', which run together gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiral metal tool is the usual device for drawing stoppers from wine bottles.

clue.text: Food obtainable after the end of the war?

definitions.text: Food obtainable after the end of the war?

parts.words: Food obtainable after the end of the war?
parts.note: VE Day marked the end of the war in Europe, so food that became gettable then is punningly 'VE-gettables'

explanation.walkthrough: VE stands for Victory in Europe, 8 May 1945; read the answer as VE + 'gettables'.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden produce such as carrots and cabbage is an everyday kind of food.

clue.text: Relative makes a sarcastic remark after changing gear

indicators.note: after puts the taunt after the reordered letters
changing says the letters of gear are reordered

parts.note: a taunt is a jeering remark

explanation.surface: A family member sneers after shifting gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-aunt is a parent's aunt, a family relative.

clue.text: Still a man even if he loses the order

definitions.text: Still a man even if he loses the order

parts.words: Still a man even if he loses the order
parts.note: a monastic order named after a saint can lose its ending and leave the saint's name, also a word for a newly married man

explanation.walkthrough: The Benedictine order loses its last three letters to leave the saint's name; a benedict is also a newly married man.
explanation.definitionFit: The founder of the Benedictine order was a man; shorn of -ine, the order leaves his name.

clue.text: More sanctimonious at the seaside?

definitions.meaning: pi is crossword slang for pious, so piously sanctimonious comparative adds -er
a seaside resort's jetty jutting out to sea, with its amusements

explanation.walkthrough: PI is an informal British word for sanctimonious, so 'more pi' gives the first sense; British seaside towns have long promenade jetties.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the comparative of pi, pious; the other is a seaside jetty.

clue.text: Acted badly after due revision although trained

indicators.note: after puts the second rearrangement after the first
revision says the letters of due are revised into a new order
badly says the letters of acted are scrambled

explanation.surface: A performer hammed it up after reworking was due, despite training.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams: 'revision' works on due and 'badly' on Acted; 'although' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone educated has been schooled and instructed, trained.

clue.text: Look for a match

definitions.meaning: to gaze closely or squint at something
an equal, someone who matches another in rank or ability

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to gaze hard; the other is an equal in standing.

clue.text: In turning red I entertain an embarrassing element

indicators.note: In at the start says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to blushing while hosting, an awkward part of the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'turnING RED I ENTertain'; 'an embarrassing' only dresses the surface around the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingredient is a component part of a mixture, so an element of it.

clue.text: A plant may have one to compete with me

parts.note: to race is to compete
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener's plant could take him on in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A raceme is a flower cluster with flowers on short stalks along a central stem.

clue.text: When around let become a foreigner

indicators.note: become says the letters of the two words change into a new shape

explanation.surface: Advice on when an incomer might be allowed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When' is a link word, and 'let' looks like a verb of permission but is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlander is a stranger from another land, an alien.

clue.text: Weapon caught in a shower if left outside

indicators.note: caught in says the answer is trapped within the words that follow

explanation.surface: An arm gets soaked in a downpour if left out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'showeR IF LEft'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled firearm, a weapon.

clue.text: Key personnel have to worry about a penny

indicators.note: about tells us the word for worry surrounds the penny

parts.note: care means anxiety or concern
D was the abbreviation for an old British penny, from the Latin denarius

explanation.surface: Essential staff fret over a single coin.
explanation.walkthrough: D stood for the penny in pre-decimal British money; 'have to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a core group of trained people forming the nucleus of an organisation.

clue.text: Anger in a medical man is more dreadful

indicators.note: in places the anger inside the doctor

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
ire means anger

explanation.surface: Fury in a doctor makes things worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire means dreadful or terrible, and this is its comparative.

clue.text: Universal love transformed into undeveloped seed

indicators.note: transformed says the letters are changed into a new order

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: Love for all becomes the start of new life in a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: In botany an ovule is the structure that becomes a seed after fertilisation.

clue.text: Where to eat when there is a celebration in the old country

indicators.note: in places the celebration inside the ancient land

parts.note: Caria was an ancient region in south-west Asia Minor
a fete is a festival or party

explanation.surface: A dining spot found where a party is held back in the homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the old country' sounds like a nostalgic homeland but means an ancient one, CARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-service restaurant is a place for meals.

clue.text: Catch a woman lower

parts.note: to net is to catch, as with fish
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Trap a lady lower down.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether is an old word meaning lower or underneath, as in the nether regions.

clue.text: A policeman is needed to disperse danger ahead of me

indicators.note: ahead of puts the scrambled letters before the word me
to disperse says the letters of danger are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An officer is called to break up a threat before it reaches the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a French police officer.
